purpose: Offline Lowtide mezzanine timber material candidate
original_prompt:
Use case: photorealistic-natural
Asset type: seamless diffuse/base-colour texture for a realistic game environment, 2048 x 2048 square.
Primary request: an orthographic, perfectly top-down material scan of an old North German port warehouse's heavy, worn pine floor. Eight broad horizontal floorboard courses, each approximately 250 mm wide, spanning a 3 metre length. Long structural planks with staggered tight butt joints, very fine dark 2–3 mm gaps. A few small dark square nail heads near the butt joints, not decorative rows.
Materials/textures: dense straight pine grain, restrained knots, pale abrasion in the high grain, shallow dents and longitudinal scuffs from moving cargo. Weathered muted grey-brown and warm taupe, low saturation; gentle variation between boards. A maintained working warehouse, worn and dry with subtle ingrained dirt, not rotten, splintery, or wet.
Lighting: uniform cross-polarised diffuse illumination; no directional shadows, highlights, ambient vignette, perspective, bevel lighting, or baked 3D shading. Preserve natural fine photographic wood detail.
Composition: edge-to-edge material only. Straight horizontal board courses, no perspective or border. Perfectly seamless repeat on all four edges: board boundaries and grain continue across left/right edges; the top and bottom edges meet within one continuous board course. Avoid a dark outer outline. Butt joints are staggered naturally and never form a repeating staircase pattern.
Avoid: domestic laminate/parquet, narrow boards, orange varnish, very dark grain stripes, deep black trenches, high contrast individual boards, painted markings, text, logos, objects, captions.
atlas_edit_prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: wood scan atlas for individual warehouse floorboards in a game material.
Edit target: supplied worn pine texture.
Preserve the photographic muted grey-brown wood, restrained knots and worn grain, the eight horizontal plank rows, square framing and flat diffuse lighting.
Remove only the vertical butt joints and square nail heads inside the horizontal rows, continuing the adjacent wood grain through their former positions. Each of the eight rows must be one uninterrupted long board running fully from the left edge to the right edge. Keep the seven narrow horizontal gaps separating rows. Keep all rows perfectly straight and the same height.
This image will be sampled as an atlas, one entire row per physical board; it does not need to repeat at the image edges. No border, perspective, bevel lighting, specular highlights, text, objects, dramatic scratches or exaggerated grain.

unused_repeat_experiment.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: seamless PBR base-colour texture for a game warehouse floor.
Edit target: supplied old pine floor texture.
Keep the muted grey-brown colour, realistic grain, worn surface, square nail heads, flat diffuse lighting, straight horizontal boards and eight-course layout.
Change only the boundary construction so the image tiles naturally in both directions. Put half of a very narrow, dark floorboard joint along the top edge and the matching other half along the bottom edge: when repeated vertically, every board must have exactly the same roughly one-eighth-image width. Do not combine the first and last boards into one double-width board. Make all internal horizontal joints meet the left/right boundaries at exactly equal heights. Blend the wood grain at the left and right edge so it continues across a horizontal tile repeat, without a vertical colour seam.
Keep tight 2–3 mm board joints, subtle board-to-board colour variation, 3 m horizontal by 2 m vertical physical coverage. No border, vignette, lighting gradient, captions, objects or text.
unused_repeat_experiment.reason: Atlas sampling is used instead; this repeat edit is not part of the candidate.
